subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & quality concerns / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Joe Bennett <joe.bennett@acmeretail.com>; neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: model fit, benchmarks, next steps

Hi Joe — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of needs
- Primary goal: generate concise product descriptions from catalog entries with strict compliance rules for legal copy.
- Throughput target: 50 qps; p50 latency target <= 250ms on dedicated capacity.
- Key quality metric: percentage of hallucinations on safety-critical fields (must be <0.5%).

What we recommended on the call
- Candidate models: OpenRedwood-2.7Q (recommended for cost/latency balance), Redbase-Long-1.4 (for long-context cases).
- Suggested config: 4-beam decoding, temperature 0.0 for deterministic outputs on legal copy, and pinned tokenizer/quantization profile.

Benchmarks & artifacts
- Preliminary benchmarks attached: benchmark_report_v1.pdf (includes latency/cost/accuracy on your sample corpus).
- Prompt set we used: prompt_set_retailco_v1.jsonl (attached).
- Live eval/drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-evals

Risks we identified
- We observed a small quality regression on one of your safety prompts when moving from model v2.2.8 -> v2.3.1 (higher rate of trailing hallucinations).
- We flagged a diff in the tokenization behavior for certain product codes that correlates with the regression.

Next steps (action items)
1) Marissa (me): share these artifacts and schedule follow-up with engineering to scope a targeted regression analysis (ETA: EOD tomorrow).
2) Rishi: run a diff run between v2.2.8 and v2.3.1 on the full prompt set and produce a prioritized list of failing prompts.
3) Joe: confirm whether you want us to hold on any planned rollout until regressions are resolved, or proceed with a pinned baseline.

If it helps, I added the HubSpot deal here: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4521.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0123

Attachment: benchmark_report_v1.pdf (summary PDF)
Attachment: prompt_set_retailco_v1.jsonl (prompt set sample)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Joe Bennett <joe.bennett@acmeretail.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, benchmarks, next steps

Thanks Marissa — good notes. A few engineering points / commitments from our side: 

- I'll kick off a focused diff evaluation between model v2.2.8 and v2.3.1 across the attached prompt_set_retailco_v1.jsonl. Goal is to surface the top 50 prompts with the largest delta in safety/precision metrics.
- Preliminary hypothesis: tokenization changes in the tokenizer-v1.8 release altered how product codes are chunked, which affected the downstream alignment heuristics.
- If the diff confirms a regression tied to tokenization or quantization, options are:
  a) Pin customer to v2.2.8 until we ship a tokenizer-compatible patch (fast, conservative).
  b) Patch the tokenizer/normalization (risky for cascade effects, slower).
  c) Apply a targeted prompt wrapper/normalizer for these product codes as a short-term mitigation.

I can have a first-pass diff report by tomorrow 10:00 AM PT. If Joe wants us to hold rollout immediately, we should treat that as high priority.

Rishi
Staff Engineer, Inference
From: Joe Bennett <joe.bennett@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@acmeretail.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, benchmarks, next steps

Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the artifacts. Our legal/product team is uncomfortable moving forward if there's an unresolved regression on safety-critical fields.

Two asks from our side: 
1) Please pause any automatic upgrades for our account (we do not want v2.3.1 applied). If you can pin us to v2.2.8 today that would be ideal.
2) Rishi — appreciate the diff. Can you include expected timeline for rollback/pinning and any impacts to throughput or latency if we pin to v2.2.8?

CC'ing contracts to ensure any change to SLO/rollout is captured in the deployment addendum.

Joe
Dir, Product — Acme Retail
joe.bennett@acmeretail.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Joe Bennett <joe.bennett@acmeretail.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, contracts@acmeretail.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, benchmarks, next steps

Joe — understood and noted. Quick reply with concrete next steps and timings: 

- Pinning: We can pin your account to v2.2.8 immediately; this is a configuration change on Dedicated and will not affect throughput. Estimated ETA: 2 hours to apply and validate.
- Diff report: Rishi will share a prioritized diff + remediation plan by tomorrow 10:00 AM PT (as he noted).
- Mitigations: In parallel, we will prototype a prompt normalizer for affected product-code patterns (short-term) and evaluate tokenizer patch risk in a separate change window.
- Documentation/update to contract: I'll ask our contracts lead to acknowledge the deployment addendum and note the pinning change — @contracts@acmeretail.com please confirm receipt and any required paperwork.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync for tomorrow 11:00 AM PT to walk through the diff findings and agree on rollback vs patch. Please let me know if that works.

Thanks —
Marissa

On the sync: https://app.hubspot.com/meeting/marissa/30min
